gaps.category: State-run programmes small operators run for the state: Medicaid/Medicare home and community-based providers, CACFP/WIC vendors
gaps.first_search: CACFP family day care home monthly claim software sponsor meal count 2026
gaps.why: Family child care and adult day care homes must file monthly CACFP meal claims and menus, and WIC-authorised small grocers have vendor rules. Huge count of micro-providers; only K21 (child care subsidy attendance) and K31 (EVV) touch this. CACFP claim and meal-count filing is a distinct duty and buyer group. I'm not sure what vendors already cover it.

gaps.category: Tobacco, alcohol and cannabis retailers: state excise, licence and track-and-trace duties
gaps.first_search: state cannabis track and trace METRC monthly tax report small licensee compliance 2026
gaps.why: Many tiny retailers file recurring state reports. Cannabis dispensaries, cultivators and craft distillers or breweries must use METRC or BioTrack manifests and monthly excise returns. K15/K16 cover only label registration and PACT. The ledger shows no retail excise, TTB or state cannabis seed-to-sale item, and none of the 38 categories covers it.

gaps.category: Local business licensing, alarm and fire-code permits (municipal)
gaps.first_search: annual fire inspection report third-party submission portal restaurants hood suppression NFPA 96 Compliance Engine small business
gaps.why: Cities require annual business licences, alarm permits and false-alarm fees, fire-inspection and hood or sprinkler certifications (NFPA 96, 25) for restaurants and small shops. Third-party inspector submission portals such as The Compliance Engine are used by contractors but not owners. Missing from the 38 categories, which cover only mobile food and building owners.

gaps.category: Trade-licence continuing education and renewal for solo contractors, and sole-trader state tax registrations (sales/use tax, workers' comp audits)
gaps.first_search: contractor license renewal continuing education tracker state board 2026 solo electrician plumber
gaps.why: Solo electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, contractors and cosmetologists face state licensing board CE and renewal cycles. Small employers also face workers' comp payroll audits and state unemployment (SUI) rate notices. Several 2024-2026 state rules may apply, including EPA Section 608 recordkeeping. The ledger has no licensing-board or SUI/workers' comp item.

gaps.category: Waste-oil, used-oil and universal-waste handlers; small quantity generators of hazardous waste (state biennial reports and EPA ID)
gaps.first_search: small quantity generator re-notification EPA ID every four years state annual hazardous waste report auto repair shop software
gaps.why: Auto repair shops, dry cleaners, salons, print shops and similar very-small-quantity generators must re-notify EPA ID every four years (SQG), and some states require annual or biennial hazardous waste reports. Used-oil collection and mercury lamp recycling records also apply. K32 covers only e-Manifest; the generator re-notification and state annual report duty is missing. Also dry cleaner (perc) and auto-body paint NESHAP rules (6H).

gaps.category: Beneficial ownership, annual reports and registered-agent filings for small entities (state LLC annual reports, Corporate Transparency Act status)
gaps.first_search: state LLC annual report deadline administrative dissolution small business 2026 Texas franchise tax no tax due report
gaps.why: Every LLC and corporation must file a state annual report or franchise tax return, and CTA/BOI rules changed in 2025 (domestic companies exempted by FinCEN in March 2025). Millions of micro firms miss deadlines and face administrative dissolution. Registered-agent services exist, so check what they cover. Also Delaware franchise tax and Texas Public Information Report. Not covered in any of the 38 categories.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Federal UST rule (40 CFR 280, in force Oct 2021) requires a documented walkthrough inspection at least every 30 days, annual release-detection and equipment testing, and 1-3 year record retention; states add their own forms and retention (AZ 1 yr, NE annual walkthrough 3 yr, MS and OR forms). Only enterprise tools found (Invenco Insite360 Comply, Seneca Compliance Manager); no small-operator app seen. See candidate C1. W&M side is known K04.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: State grain dealer/warehouse licensing exists (e.g. Wisconsin DATCP annual financial statement above 200k bushels, CPA review or audit, due 15th day of 4th month after year-end). Only the Wisconsin statute and DATCP forms were seen; no recurring small-firm filing burden worth a candidate beyond a weak note (C13). 50-state grain licensing not checked.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Nothing new. NCUA 2026 notices are paperwork renewals and a deregulatory review (AML/BSA among five areas), no new small-credit-union filing. Co-op/savings-group angle not searched beyond this.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: CLIA Certificate of Waiver is a 2-year renewal with random inspections only (about 2 percent); no 2026 change found, thin burden (C12 weak). Dental offices with amalgam duties are in C2 (cat. 31). Payer credentialing and billing not searched.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: DEA biennial inventory and electronic Form 106 (45 days after discovery of theft/loss) are existing duties; vendors such as C2 Keep cover perpetual inventory and biennial reports (C11 weak). Related known ideas K12 (MFP refunds) and K30 (DSCSA) already rejected. No new rule found.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: California is the only state with a janitorial registry (AB 1978, Labor Code 1420 ff., yearly registration, reported $500 fee, hirers fined for using unregistered contractors, 3-year payroll records). Fees and current rules unconfirmed. See C9. Healthcare staffing is K03, security guard licensing K23.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: New York Labor Law 220-j mandates electronic certified payroll for public and some private prevailing-wage projects from Jan 1 2026 (every 30 days even with no work, $100/day penalty after 14-day grace). NYSDOL portal takes manual entry or XML bulk upload per an XSD; LCPtracker already generates the NYSDOL XML (Aug/Sep 2026 release notes). See C4. NYC runs a separate database. SWPPP is known K19.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Notary electronic journal and recording retention rules (10 years in NC, OK, NY) are in state RON statutes; no 2026 change found and many e-notary platforms already provide journals. FinCEN real estate rule is K27 (enjoined). Nothing new. Broker trust-account reports not searched.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: New York statewide STR registry (registration every 2 years, in effect 2025) plus NY sales tax on STR from April 2025; Rhode Island registry since 2022; Connecticut HB 5536 (statewide registry, $100 fee, would apply 2027) with passage unconfirmed. Avalara MyLodgeTax and platform collection exist. See C6 (weak).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: FDA food facility biennial registration renewal window is open now (Oct 1 to Dec 31, 2026, free, FDA portal). TSCA 8(a)(7) PFAS reporting start moved to the earlier of 60 days after the substantive final rule or Jan 31 2027; article importers may be exempted (proposal). See C7 and C8, both weak. FSMA 204, UFLPA and Lacey Act not searched.

coverage.category: 31. Dental offices (country-specific): EPA dental amalgam rule, 40 CFR 441
coverage.found: Separators installed before June 14 2017 must be replaced by June 14 2027; ongoing visual inspection, maintenance and disposal records kept 3 years; one-time compliance report was due Oct 2020 (90 days after opening for new offices) to the local control authority or EPA. HealthFirst OnTraq and Solmetex Compliance Center exist. See C2.

coverage.category: 32. Condominium, HOA and cooperative associations (Florida statutes 718/720)
coverage.found: Florida condo associations with 25+ units must have a website or app posting records within 30 days (effective Jan 1 2026, HB 1021); HOAs with 100+ parcels since Jan 1 2025; SIRS must be posted and sent to the Division within 45 days of receipt; DBPR online account due Oct 1 2025. Many vendors (CondoControl, BuildingLink, SetMySite, MyCommunitySite). See C3.

coverage.category: 33. Mobile food vendors and cottage food operators (local and county permits)
coverage.found: Permits are per vehicle and per city/county (Monterey CA expires June 30 yearly, no auto-renewal; Jurupa Valley needs county health permit first; Texas ch. 437A multi-county rule applies only to counties over 2.1 million). No software found in the search; evidence thin. See C10 (unverified).

coverage.category: 34. Federal firearms licensees (ATF A&D bound book and Form 4473)
coverage.found: ATF 2026 proposals: electronic recordkeeping codification (comments to Aug 6 2026) and fixed 20 or 30 year retention (RIN 1140-AA95, comments to Aug 4 2026); not confirmed final. Fastbound and others already sell ATF 2016-1 compliant e-bound books. See C5 (rejected).

coverage.category: 35. Money services: check cashers and small money transmitters (state licensing via NMLS)
coverage.found: State annual assessment reports and bond adjustments run through NMLS (WA due July 1; NY check cashers annual report Mar 17 2026; WA attestation Nov 1 to Dec 31); Maine required electronic surety bonds by Jan 31 2026. No small-licensee software found. See C14 (weak).

coverage.category: 36. Independent used-car dealers (state electronic title, odometer disclosure)
coverage.found: Only incremental changes: Louisiana SB72 e-titles effective Aug 1 2026, Colorado HB26-1041 (enactment unconfirmed), Virginia optional e-title program; federal odometer disclosure for MY2011+ since 2021. No mandatory new small-dealer filing found. See C15 (weak, unverified).

coverage.category: 37. Packaging producers and article importers (state EPR, PFAS)
coverage.found: Packaging EPR in CA, CO, OR, MN, MD, WA is administered through Circular Action Alliance; 2025 supply reports were due ~May 31/June 1 2026; no 2027 dates and no small-producer thresholds found. See C7 and C8.

coverage.category: 38. Building owners under local performance and inspection laws (NYC LL97, LL87, LL126)
coverage.found: LL97 covers buildings over 25,000 sq ft; LL87 energy efficiency reports due Dec 31 2026 for the 2026 cohort; LL126 parking structure inspection cycles (2026-2027 for Bronx, Queens, Staten Island sub-cycle) apply to all garages. Consultants (Milrose, Rand, Thornton Tomasetti) own it; not scored beyond C16 (unverified).
